results.question: What is a Delaware Statutory Trust?
results.answer_text:
A Delaware Statutory Trust (DST) is an unincorporated association recognized as an entity separate from its owners under Delaware law. [1] It is created by executing a governing instrument and filing an executed certificate of trust. [2] Beneficial owners of a DST are entitled to the same limitation on personal liability as stockholders of Delaware corporations. [3] The trust may sue or be sued, and its property is subject to attachment or execution as if the trust were a corporation. [3]

Sources:
[1] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 2) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[2] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 2) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[3] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 3) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf

results.question: Can an interest in a Delaware statutory trust be acquired in a 1031 exchange?
results.answer_text:
Yes, an interest in a Delaware statutory trust can be acquired in a 1031 exchange under certain conditions. [1] The IRS has ruled that exchanging real property for an interest in a DST through a qualified intermediary qualifies as the exchange of real property for real property, not the exchange for a certificate of trust or beneficial interest that would be excluded under § 1031(a)(2)(E). [2] This treatment is based on Revenue Ruling 2004-86, which provides the framework for DSTs to qualify for 1031 exchanges. [3]

Key considerations:
- The IRS could theoretically change its stance or rule unfavorably on a specific DST offering, potentially resulting in unexpected tax liabilities. [3]
- A properly structured DST should fit well under current IRS rules, but professional guidance is important to ensure compliance. [3]

Sources:
[1] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 1) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[2] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 8) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[3] Six Risks of Delaware Statutory Trusts in 1031 Exchanges (Kiplinger, Risk No. 5: The taxman cometh (maybe)) https://www.kiplinger.com/retirement/risks-of-delaware-statutory-trusts-in-1031-exchanges

results.question: What limits does Revenue Ruling 2004-86 place on the powers of a DST trustee?
results.answer_text:
The trustee's activities are limited to the collection and distribution of income, and the trustee cannot exchange the property for other assets, purchase additional assets beyond specified short-term investments, or accept additional contributions to the DST. [1] The trustee cannot renegotiate the terms of the debt used to acquire the property or renegotiate leases with tenants except in cases of bankruptcy or insolvency. [1] The trustee is restricted to making only minor non-structural modifications to the property unless required by law. [1] The trustee's investment powers are limited to short-term obligations that mature before the next distribution date, which must be held until maturity, preventing the trustee from varying the investment to benefit from market fluctuations. [2][3]

Key considerations:
- These limitations are designed to ensure the DST qualifies as an investment trust rather than a business entity for tax purposes. [1]
- The trustee may engage in ministerial activities required to maintain and operate the DST under local law. [4]

Sources:
[1] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 7) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[2] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 5) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[3] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 2) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf
[4] Revenue Ruling 2004-86 (Delaware statutory trusts and § 1031) (Internal Revenue Service (Internal Revenue Bulletin 2004-33; copy hosted by U.S. Treasury), p. 2) https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/archive-documents/rr0486.pdf

results.question: What is a 721 exchange into an UPREIT?
results.answer_text:
A 721 exchange into an UPREIT is a tax-deferred transaction where a property owner contributes their property to an operating partnership (OP) in exchange for OP Units, without triggering immediate capital gains taxes. [1] The contributed properties retain their original tax basis, and the embedded taxable gains are deferred until the OP Units are converted to REIT shares, sold, or redeemed for cash. [1] This structure allows investors to gain diversification through a professionally managed portfolio of institutional-quality real estate while deferring capital gains taxes that would be triggered through a cash sale. [2]

Key considerations:
- The exchange from OP Units to cash or REIT common shares may be a taxable event. [2]
- OP Unitholders have more complex tax reporting requirements, receiving Schedule K-1 allocations and potentially needing to file state tax returns in multiple jurisdictions. [3]
- Upon death, OP Units may receive a step-up in tax basis to current valuations, providing estate planning benefits. [2]

Sources:
[1] 721 Exchange/UPREIT (Franklin Templeton, p. 1) https://www.franklintempleton.com/forms-literature/download/721-FL
[2] 721 Exchange/UPREIT (Franklin Templeton, p. 1) https://www.franklintempleton.com/forms-literature/download/721-FL
[3] 721 Exchange/UPREIT (Franklin Templeton, p. 1) https://www.franklintempleton.com/forms-literature/download/721-FL

Note: The exchange from OP Units to cash or REIT common shares may be a taxable event.
Upon death of the OP Unitholder, the OP Units may receive a step-up in tax basis (to current valuations at date of death) and heirs then receive a higher basis in the OP Units.

results.question: What is a real estate investment trust?
results.answer_text:
A real estate investment trust (REIT) is a company that owns and typically operates income-producing real estate or related assets, allowing individuals to invest in large-scale, income-producing real estate. [1] These assets may include office buildings, shopping malls, apartments, hotels, resorts, self-storage facilities, warehouses, and mortgages or loans. [1] Unlike other real estate companies, REITs do not develop properties to resell them but instead buy and develop properties primarily to operate them as part of their own investment portfolio. [1]

Sources:
[1] Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Investor.gov), What are REITs?) https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/real-estate-investment-trusts-reits
